findings.evidence:
**Mutant S3f** (`except (binascii.Error, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):` narrowed to `except binascii.Error:`):
- Both RED files: `[pyt] tag=rv2sec-mut-S3f start=2026-10-18 04:13:08 end=2026-10-18 04:13:14 elapsed=6s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, "119 passed". SURVIVED; restore sha OK.

**What leaks under S3f** (probe_keys.py loads the module by path; [py] probe_S3f 04:13:23 rc=0):

findings.title: The key probe over 32 forms finds 0 leaks on the committed bytes, in both functions and in every log line
findings.evidence:
`[py] probe_head start=2026-10-18 04:11:08 end=2026-10-18 04:11:09 rc=0`, result "TOTAL_LEAK=0 NON_ASCII_DECODED=[]".

**What runs:** each of the 32 forms goes through `_normalise_private_key`, `build_client_secret` (the stripped value, as `_siwa_config` gives it), `exchange_authorization_code` and `revoke_refresh_token` (MockTransport, log capture).

**What is searched:** 16-character base64 windows of every generated key body (P-256 PKCS#8, SEC1, P-384, RSA, Ed25519, encrypted) and of each base64 input, plus 8-byte windows of the raw DER. The search covers str, repr, args (bytes args too), `__notes__`, the `.object` and `vars()` attributes, the whole `__context__` / `__cause__` chain, `traceback.format_exception` output and every log message.

**Detector control:** the previous bytes c1a10e40 give TOTAL_LEAK=2998 (BOM, smart-quote, en-dash armour, ZWSP and BOM-base64 forms, plus base64-of-DER and bare-body). The detector works.

**Results per form on the committed bytes:**
- **Accepted, OK in all four calls:** PEM with real newlines, PEM with literal backslash-n, base64, base64 wrapped at 76, CRLF, SEC1 EC PEM, and an NBSP-wrapped PEM (see RV2-SEC-6).
- **Constant ValueError** (chain=1, b64dec=0, jwtenc=0): BOM, smart quotes, trailing U+201D, en-dash armour, ZWSP prefix, ZWSP in the body, NBSP in the body, NBSP for newlines, BOM + base64.
- **Constant ValueError, one base64 decode:** labelled PEM raw, base64 of a labelled PEM, base64url, base64 of DER, base64 of garbage, garbage, bare body.
- **Library errors with clean chains:** RSA, Ed25519 and P-384 give InvalidKeyError; encrypted and base64-of-encrypted give TypeError; a public key gives AttributeError; the three truncated forms give a cryptography ValueError (chain=2, LEAK=0).

**Logs:** every failing form logs exactly two WARNING lines `[SIWA] client secret build failed: <Type>` (one from the exchange, one from the revoke), with exc_info=0, logLEAK=0 and 0 sends. Every accepted form logs INFO `exchange status=200` and `revoke attempt=1 status=200`.

**Coverage of these forms by committed rows:**
- R3 covers: pem-real-newlines, pem-literal-backslash-n, base64, base64-wrapped-76, pem-space-joined, garbage, rsa, bom-pem, smart-quoted-pem, zwsp-pem (prefix) and base64-of-labelled-pem.
- R9 covers garbage-key.
- en-dash armour, BOM-base64 and NBSP/ZWSP prefixes are the same code path as bom-pem, pinned by the S3d spy kill.
- base64url, raw labelled PEM and base64 of garbage are the same path as garbage (binascii.Error).
- Ed25519, P-384, public key, encrypted and truncated are library errors from `jwt.encode` with no module code to mutate; rsa covers the class and all measured 0 leak.
- Uncovered classes: RV2-SEC-1 (DER) and RV2-SEC-2 (armour-prefixed non-ASCII).

findings.title: An NBSP-wrapped PEM is accepted: str.strip() removes Unicode whitespace before the ASCII check
findings.evidence:
probe_head form nbsp-wrapped-pem (U+00A0 + PEM + U+00A0):
- Both functions return OK, the exchange succeeds and the revoke succeeds.
- `_siwa_config` and `_normalise_private_key` both call `.strip()`, which removes U+00A0 (as it does U+2028 and U+3000; BOM and ZWSP are not whitespace and are refused).
- What gets decoded is pure ASCII, so no non-ASCII text is ever decoded (NON_ASCII_DECODED=[]) and the leak count is 0.
